rig: A Linux PC, each box fed by a USB device emulator on its USB3, both boxes behind one USB hub and tested one at a time

layers.wire: USB packets on the PC's bus, timed by the kernel's usbmon
layers.evdev: Input events, timed by the kernel as the HID driver handles each report
layers.hidraw: Each report byte for byte, timed when the reading program wakes
layers.host: The PC's clock, read by the test program when it writes a command, or when the clone connects or disconnects
layers.emulator: Native reports as the emulator queued them, on its clock, placed on the bus clock through its control link's packets (usbmon)

defects.text: A report descriptor longer than 512 bytes isn't served, so the PC's HID driver doesn't load for that clone.
A request for the HID class descriptor gets a STALL instead of the native reply.
While it injects, stock reads a 1 kHz mouse whose motion varies about 460 times a second instead of 1,000, at 10 to 1,000 moves a second.
A move or click sent to a new clone before its first native report is lost: none of 3 tries arrived within 1 s.
After the PC turns the clone's port off and on, stock holds the first move for over 1 s in 6 of 10 tries.
A button a program pressed stays held after the program closes the port, until another program releases it or the box restarts.
Default moves at 1,000 a second into a moving 1 kHz mouse lose counts: 10 and 13 of 15,000 in two runs.
When the PC switches the clone's configuration, stock reconnects the clone instead of passing the switch to the real device: 3 of 3 tries.
One write of 30 binary moves, moves clumped 32 to a write, or moves written back to back lose commands and leave stock's parser one command behind until a power cycle.
While the PC sleeps, neither an injected move nor the real device's remote wakeup wakes it.
